steps.say: Diagnosing polycystic ovary syndrome requires fulfilling Rotterdam consensus criteria after excluding mimic conditions. Diagnosis demands at least 2 of 3 features across anovulation, androgen excess, and polycystic morphology.
steps.tx: According to the **PCOS Guideline 2023** and **Rotterdam criteria**, diagnosing polycystic ovary syndrome requires meeting at least 2 of 3 features: clinical or biochemical **hyperandrogenism**, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology, following rigorous exclusion of thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia, and non-classical congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

steps.say: Updated ultrasound thresholds reflect higher resolution modern transvaginal transducers. Current criteria require at least 20 follicles per ovary or ovarian volume reaching 10 mL.
steps.tx: Updated international sonographic **PCOM criteria** require a **follicle number per ovary** of at least 20 follicles measuring 2 to 9 mm in either ovary using high-frequency transducers (>=8 MHz), or an increased **ovarian volume** of at least 10 mL in the absence of corpora lutea.

left.title: Follicle Number Per Ovary (FNPO)
points: Do not use in adolescents <8 years post-menarche

right.title: Ovarian Volume Cutoff
points: Reliable indicator if transabdominal scan used

steps.say: Serum anti-Mullerian hormone now provides a recognized diagnostic substitute for ultrasound. In adults, elevated AMH can define polycystic morphology without transvaginal scanning.
steps.tx: The 2023 international guidelines formally endorse serum AMH as an accurate **substitute for ultrasound** to define polycystic morphology in adult women. Utilizing **AMH for PCOM** as a validated **PCOS diagnostic biomarker** streamlines assessment, particularly in patients where transvaginal ultrasonography is impractical or declined: **PCOS biomarker 2023**.

nodes.label: Adult female presenting with suspected PCOS
Assessment of ovulatory function and androgen levels
Serum AMH test substitutes for pelvic ultrasound

steps.say: Premature ovarian insufficiency represents early loss of ovarian activity before age 40. Diagnostic criteria demand at least 4 months of oligomenorrhea alongside elevated gonadotropins.
steps.tx: Establishing a diagnosis of **premature ovarian insufficiency** requires oligo- or amenorrhea for at least 4 months before **age 40**, confirmed by documented **FSH >25 IU/L** on two independent occasions drawn at least 4 to 6 weeks apart. Comprehensive assessment and rigorous clinical monitoring ensure optimal outcomes across every assisted reproductive technology protocol in modern practice.

steps.say: Genetic causes account for up to 20 percent of premature ovarian failure cases. Clinical workup mandates peripheral blood karyotyping and fragile X premutation testing.
steps.tx: A verified genetic etiology underlies 10 to 20 percent of cases, requiring baseline cytogenetic karyotyping to detect **Turner mosaicism 45,X** or structural X rearrangements. Molecular testing for **FMR1 premutation** (55 to 200 CGG trinucleotide repeats) is mandatory to rule out **Fragile X**-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome risk.

nodes.label: POI confirmed by repeat FSH >25 IU/L
FMR1 triplet repeat sizing (55 to 200 CGG repeats)

steps.say: Autoimmune destruction of steroidogenic tissue requires targeted laboratory screening. Testing for 21-hydroxylase antibodies identifies women at risk for polyglandular Addisonian failure.
steps.tx: Diagnosing **autoimmune POI** requires screening for adrenal cortex autoantibodies or **anti-21-hydroxylase** antibodies (anti-21OH). Positive serology flags subclinical autoimmune adrenalitis, necessitating endocrine surveillance for autoimmune **polyglandular syndrome** alongside testing for thyroid peroxidase autoantibodies. Comprehensive assessment and rigorous clinical monitoring ensure optimal outcomes across every assisted reproductive technology protocol in modern practice.

steps.say: Patients with premature ovarian failure should be counseled that conception remains possible. Between 5 and 10 percent of women experience spontaneous pregnancy from intermittent follicular activity.
steps.tx: Patients diagnosed with POI must be reassured that ovarian function can fluctuate unpredictably. Spontaneous ovulation occurs in up to 20 percent of women with **idiopathic POI**, culminating in **spontaneous conception in POI** in 5 to 10 percent of patients through **intermittent ovulation**.

right.title: Spontaneous Clinical Conception
points: Occurs in 5 to 10 percent of idiopathic cases
Barrier contraception advised if pregnancy unwanted
Oocyte donation remains definitive ART choice

steps.say: Continuous hormone replacement therapy is vital to prevent cardiovascular and skeletal morbidity. Transdermal estradiol combined with cyclic progesterone must continue until natural menopause age.
steps.tx: Immediate **hormone replacement therapy** is mandatory to prevent premature osteoporosis and ischemic heart disease. First-line therapy uses **transdermal estradiol** (100 mcg patch) paired with micronized oral progesterone for 12 to 14 days monthly, continued until the **natural menopause age** of roughly 50 to 52 years: **17-beta estradiol**.

rows: Avoids first-pass hepatic metabolism, neutral VTE risk
Oral micronized progesterone 200 mg x 14 days
Adequate calcium (1000 mg) and Vitamin D
